questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 14 cm and a height of 6 cm. Take your time — what is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 14 × 6 = 42 cm². Halving is the step that's easy to rush past.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 2 cm and height 6 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14)

block.label: Scrub It
block.sub: Rub out the wrong answers with your finger

questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2(3.14)(4) + 2(3.14)(2)(6) = 25.1 + 75.4 = 100.5 cm². You need both the ends and the curved surface.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: If 40g of reactants react fully inside a sealed container, what is the mass of the products?
questions.why: Mass is conserved in a closed system, so the products weigh exactly the same as the reactants — 40g.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What word describes a chemical reaction that feels cold as it happens?
questions.why: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from its surroundings, so the mixture feels cold — the opposite of an exothermic reaction.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: On a nutrition label, what unit is the energy value usually given in?
questions.why: Energy on an Australian nutrition label is measured in kilojoules (kJ), not grams — grams are used for nutrients like fat or protein, not energy.
